Start with the object supplied to your component:"},{"line":31,"text":""},{"line":32,"text":"| You already have | Read this contract first | Read implementation details when |"},{"line":33,"text":"|---|---|---|"},{"line":34,"text":"| An existing `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback | [`mountSpendingView`](causal-view-binding.ts): five latest port values, explicit `unavailable` ports, observation cleanup | You need a different observation policy; the [ordinary panel](causal-ordinary-panel.ts) shows a consumer |"},{"line":35,"text":"| A Graph and prepared creation inputs | [`spendingAlertsFor`](causal-entry.ts): immutable defaults, per-compose overrides and returned view/capabilities | You also own input preparation or the executing host; follow [inputs](causal-inputs.ts) or [host](causal-focused-host.ts) for those responsibilities |"},{"line":36,"text":"| Issued capabilities, their owning Graph and expected binding | [`assertCausalCapabilities`](../../packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/capabilities.ts): issued-object, Graph, binding and lineage validation | You implement capability construction; the [role examples](causal-audience.examples.ts) show consumption |"},{"line":37,"text":"| The owning Graph and a running instance | [Inspect one instance in a shared graph](#inspect-one-instance-in-a-shared-graph): full structure plus that instance's host and retained evidence | You are tracing a specific readiness, admission or outcome dependency |"},{"line":38,"text":""},{"line":39,"text":"Using an existing view does not require reconstructing its input facts, permission"},{"line":40,"text":"sources or host. Start with the object supplied to your component:"},{"line":31,"text":""},{"line":32,"text":"| You already have | Read this contract first | Read implementation details when |"},{"line":33,"text":"|---|---|---|"},{"line":34,"text":"| An existing `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback | [`mountSpendingView`](causal-view-binding.ts): five latest port values, explicit `unavailable` ports, observation cleanup | You need a different observation policy; the [ordinary panel](causal-ordinary-panel.ts) shows a consumer |"},{"line":35,"text":"| A Graph and prepared creation inputs | [`spendingAlertsFor`](causal-entry.ts): immutable defaults, per-compose overrides and returned view/capabilities | You also own input preparation or the executing host; follow [inputs](causal-inputs.ts) or [host](causal-focused-host.ts) for those responsibilities |"},{"line":36,"text":"| Issued capabilities, their owning Graph and expected binding | [`assertCausalCapabilities`](../../packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/capabilities.ts): issued-object, Graph, binding and lineage validation | You implement capability construction; the [role examples](causal-audience.examples.ts) show consumption |"},{"line":37,"text":"| The owning Graph and a running instance | [Inspect one instance in a shared graph](#inspect-one-instance-in-a-shared-graph): full structure plus that instance's host and retained evidence | You are tracing a specific readiness, admission or outcome dependency |"},{"line":38,"text":""},{"line":39,"text":"Using an existing view does not require reconstructing its input facts, permission"},{"line":40,"text":"sources or host. Start with the object supplied to your component:"},{"line":31,"text":""},{"line":32,"text":"| You already have | Read this contract first | Read implementation details when |"},{"line":33,"text":"|---|---|---|"},{"line":34,"text":"| An existing `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback | [`mountSpendingView`](causal-view-binding.ts): five latest port values, explicit `unavailable` ports, observation cleanup | You need a different observation policy; the [ordinary panel](causal-ordinary-panel.ts) shows a consumer |"},{"line":35,"text":"| A Graph and prepared creation inputs | [`spendingAlertsFor`](causal-entry.ts): immutable defaults, per-compose overrides and returned view/capabilities | You also own input preparation or the executing host; follow [inputs](causal-inputs.ts) or [host](causal-focused-host.ts) for those responsibilities |"},{"line":36,"text":"| Issued capabilities, their owning Graph and expected binding | [`assertCausalCapabilities`](../../packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/capabilities.ts): issued-object, Graph, binding and lineage validation | You implement capability construction; the [role examples](causal-audience.examples.ts) show consumption |"},{"line":37,"text":"| The owning Graph and a running instance | [Inspect one instance in a shared graph](#inspect-one-instance-in-a-shared-graph): full structure plus that instance's host and retained evidence | You are tracing a specific readiness, admission or outcome dependency |"},{"line":38,"text":""},{"line":39,"text":"Using an existing view does not require reconstructing its input facts, permission"},{"line":40,"text":"sources or host. Start with the object supplied to your component:"},{"line":31,"text":""},{"line":32,"text":"| You already have | Read this contract first | Read implementation details when |"},{"line":33,"text":"|---|---|---|"},{"line":34,"text":"| An existing `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback | [`mountSpendingView`](causal-view-binding.ts): five latest port values, explicit `unavailable` ports, observation cleanup | You need a different observation policy; the [ordinary panel](causal-ordinary-panel.ts) shows a consumer |"},{"line":35,"text":"| A Graph and prepared creation inputs | [`spendingAlertsFor`](causal-entry.ts): immutable defaults, per-compose overrides and returned view/capabilities | You also own input preparation or the executing host; follow [inputs](causal-inputs.ts) or [host](causal-focused-host.ts) for those responsibilities |"},{"line":36,"text":"| Issued capabilities, their owning Graph and expected binding | [`assertCausalCapabilities`](../../packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/capabilities.ts): issued-object, Graph, binding and lineage validation | You implement capability construction; the [role examples](causal-audience.examples.ts) show consumption |"},{"line":37,"text":"| The owning Graph and a running instance | [Inspect one instance in a shared graph](#inspect-one-instance-in-a-shared-graph): full structure plus that instance's host and retained evidence | You are tracing a specific readiness, admission or outcome dependency |"},{"line":38,"text":""},{"line":39,"text":"Using an existing view does not require reconstructing its input facts, permission"},{"line":40,"text":"sources or host. Start with the object supplied to your component:"},{"line":31,"text":""},{"line":32,"text":"| You already have | Read this contract first | Read implementation details when |"},{"line":33,"text":"|---|---|---|"},{"line":34,"text":"| An existing `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback | [`mountSpendingView`](causal-view-binding.ts): five latest port values, explicit `unavailable` ports, observation cleanup | You need a different observation policy; the [ordinary panel](causal-ordinary-panel.ts) shows a consumer |"},{"line":35,"text":"| A Graph and prepared creation inputs | [`spendingAlertsFor`](causal-entry.ts): immutable defaults, per-compose overrides and returned view/capabilities | You also own input preparation or the executing host; follow [inputs](causal-inputs.ts) or [host](causal-focused-host.ts) for those responsibilities |"},{"line":36,"text":"| Issued capabilities, their owning Graph and expected binding | [`assertCausalCapabilities`](../../packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/capabilities.ts): issued-object, Graph, binding and lineage validation | You implement capability construction; the [role examples](causal-audience.examples.ts) show consumption |"},{"line":37,"text":"| The owning Graph and a running instance | [Inspect one instance in a shared graph](#inspect-one-instance-in-a-shared-graph): full structure plus that instance's host and retained evidence | You are tracing a specific readiness, admission or outcome dependency |"},{"line":38,"text":""},{"line":39,"text":"Using an existing view does not require reconstructing its input facts, permission"},{"line":40,"text":"sources or host. Start with the object supplied to your component:"},{"line":31,"text":""},{"line":32,"text":"| You already have | Read this contract first | Read implementation details when |"},{"line":33,"text":"|---|---|---|"},{"line":34,"text":"| An existing `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback | [`mountSpendingView`](causal-view-binding.ts): five latest port values, explicit `unavailable` ports, observation cleanup | You need a different observation policy; the [ordinary panel](causal-ordinary-panel.ts) shows a consumer |"},{"line":35,"text":"| A Graph and prepared creation inputs | [`spendingAlertsFor`](causal-entry.ts): immutable defaults, per-compose overrides and returned view/capabilities | You also own input preparation or the executing host; follow [inputs](causal-inputs.ts) or [host](causal-focused-host.ts) for those responsibilities |"},{"line":36,"text":"| Issued capabilities, their owning Graph and expected binding | [`assertCausalCapabilities`](../../packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/capabilities.ts): issued-object, Graph, binding and lineage validation | You implement capability construction; the [role examples](causal-audience.examples.ts) show consumption |"},{"line":37,"text":"| The owning Graph and a running instance | [Inspect one instance in a shared graph](#inspect-one-instance-in-a-shared-graph): full structure plus that instance's host and retained evidence | You are tracing a specific readiness, admission or outcome dependency |"},{"line":38,"text":""},{"line":39,"text":"Using an existing view does not require reconstructing its input facts, permission"},{"line":40,"text":"sources or host. Start with the object supplied to your component:"},{"line":31,"text":""},{"line":32,"text":"| You already have | Read this contract first | Read implementation details when |"},{"line":33,"text":"|---|---|---|"},{"line":34,"text":"| An existing `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback | [`mountSpendingView`](causal-view-binding.ts): five latest port values, explicit `unavailable` ports, observation cleanup | You need a different observation policy; the [ordinary panel](causal-ordinary-panel.ts) shows a consumer |"},{"line":35,"text":"| A Graph and prepared creation inputs | [`spendingAlertsFor`](causal-entry.ts): immutable defaults, per-compose overrides and returned view/capabilities | You also own input preparation or the executing host; follow [inputs](causal-inputs.ts) or [host](causal-focused-host.ts) for those responsibilities |"},{"line":36,"text":"| Issued capabilities, their owning Graph and expected binding | [`assertCausalCapabilities`](../../packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/capabilities.ts): issued-object, Graph, binding and lineage validation | You implement capability construction; the [role examples](causal-audience.examples.ts) show consumption |"},{"line":37,"text":"| The owning Graph and a running instance | [Inspect one instance in a shared graph](#inspect-one-instance-in-a-shared-graph): full structure plus that instance's host and retained evidence | You are tracing a specific readiness, admission or outcome dependency |"},{"line":38,"text":""},{"line":39,"text":"Using an existing view does not require reconstructing its input facts, permission"},{"line":40,"text":"sources or host. Start with the object supplied to your component:"},{"line":31,"text":""},{"line":32,"text":"| You already have | Read this contract first | Read implementation details when |"},{"line":33,"text":"|---|---|---|"},{"line":34,"text":"| An existing `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback | [`mountSpendingView`](causal-view-binding.ts): five latest port values, explicit `unavailable` ports, observation cleanup | You need a different observation policy; the [ordinary panel](causal-ordinary-panel.ts) shows a consumer |"},{"line":35,"text":"| A Graph and prepared creation inputs | [`spendingAlertsFor`](causal-entry.ts): immutable defaults, per-compose overrides and returned view/capabilities | You also own input preparation or the executing host; follow [inputs](causal-inputs.ts) or [host](causal-focused-host.ts) for those responsibilities |"},{"line":36,"text":"| Issued capabilities, their owning Graph and expected binding | [`assertCausalCapabilities`](../../packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/capabilities.ts): issued-object, Graph, binding and lineage validation | You implement capability construction; the [role examples](causal-audience.examples.ts) show consumption |"},{"line":37,"text":"| The owning Graph and a running instance | [Inspect one instance in a shared graph](#inspect-one-instance-in-a-shared-graph): full structure plus that instance's host and retained evidence | You are tracing a specific readiness, admission or outcome dependency |"},{"line":38,"text":""},{"line":39,"text":"Using an existing view does not require reconstructing its input facts, permission"},{"line":40,"text":"sources or host. Start with the object supplied to your component:"},{"line":31,"text":""},{"line":32,"text":"| You already have | Read this contract first | Read implementation details when |"},{"line":33,"text":"|---|---|---|"},{"line":34,"text":"| An existing `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback | [`mountSpendingView`](causal-view-binding.ts): five latest port values, explicit `unavailable` ports, observation cleanup | You need a different observation policy; the [ordinary panel](causal-ordinary-panel.ts) shows a consumer |"},{"line":35,"text":"| A Graph and prepared creation inputs | [`spendingAlertsFor`](causal-entry.ts): immutable defaults, per-compose overrides and returned view/capabilities | You also own input preparation or the executing host; follow [inputs](causal-inputs.ts) or [host](causal-focused-host.ts) for those responsibilities |"},{"line":36,"text":"| Issued capabilities, their owning Graph and expected binding | [`assertCausalCapabilities`](../../packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/capabilities.ts): issued-object, Graph, binding and lineage validation | You implement capability construction; the [role examples](causal-audience.examples.ts) show consumption |"},{"line":37,"text":"| The owning Graph and a running instance | [Inspect one instance in a shared graph](#inspect-one-instance-in-a-shared-graph): full structure plus that instance's host and retained evidence | You are tracing a specific readiness, admission or outcome dependency |"},{"line":38,"text":""},{"line":39,"text":"Using an existing view does not require reconstructing its input facts, permission"},{"line":40,"text":"sources or host. Start with the object supplied to your component:"},{"line":31,"text":""},{"line":32,"text":"| You already have | Read this contract first | Read implementation details when |"},{"line":33,"text":"|---|---|---|"},{"line":34,"text":"| An existing `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback | [`mountSpendingView`](causal-view-binding.ts): five latest port values, explicit `unavailable` ports, observation cleanup | You need a different observation policy; the [ordinary panel](causal-ordinary-panel.ts) shows a consumer |"},{"line":35,"text":"| A Graph and prepared creation inputs | [`spendingAlertsFor`](causal-entry.ts): immutable defaults, per-compose overrides and returned view/capabilities | You also own input preparation or the executing host; follow [inputs](causal-inputs.ts) or [host](causal-focused-host.ts) for those responsibilities |"},{"line":36,"text":"| Issued capabilities, their owning Graph and expected binding | [`assertCausalCapabilities`](../../packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/capabilities.ts): issued-object, Graph, binding and lineage validation | You implement capability construction; the [role examples](causal-audience.examples.ts) show consumption |"},{"line":37,"text":"| The owning Graph and a running instance | [Inspect one instance in a shared graph](#inspect-one-instance-in-a-shared-graph): full structure plus that instance's host and retained evidence | You are tracing a specific readiness, admission or outcome dependency |"},{"line":38,"text":""},{"line":39,"text":"Using an existing view does not require reconstructing its input facts, permission"},{"line":40,"text":"sources or host. Start with the object supplied to your component:"},{"line":31,"text":""},{"line":32,"text":"| You already have | Read this contract first | Read implementation details when |"},{"line":33,"text":"|---|---|---|"},{"line":34,"text":"| An existing `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback | [`mountSpendingView`](causal-view-binding.ts): five latest port values, explicit `unavailable` ports, observation cleanup | You need a different observation policy; the [ordinary panel](causal-ordinary-panel.ts) shows a consumer |"},{"line":35,"text":"| A Graph and prepared creation inputs | [`spendingAlertsFor`](causal-entry.ts): immutable defaults, per-compose overrides and returned view/capabilities | You also own input preparation or the executing host; follow [inputs](causal-inputs.ts) or [host](causal-focused-host.ts) for those responsibilities |"},{"line":36,"text":"| Issued capabilities, their owning Graph and expected binding | [`assertCausalCapabilities`](../../packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/capabilities.ts): issued-object, Graph, binding and lineage validation | You implement capability construction; the [role examples](causal-audience.examples.ts) show consumption |"},{"line":37,"text":"| The owning Graph and a running instance | [Inspect one instance in a shared graph](#inspect-one-instance-in-a-shared-graph): full structure plus that instance's host and retained evidence | You are tracing a specific readiness, admission or outcome dependency |"},{"line":38,"text":""},{"line":39,"text":"Using an existing view does not require reconstructing its input facts, permission"},{"line":40,"text":"sources or host. Start with the object supplied to your component:"},{"line":31,"text":""},{"line":32,"text":"| You already have | Read this contract first | Read implementation details when |"},{"line":33,"text":"|---|---|---|"},{"line":34,"text":"| An existing `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback | [`mountSpendingView`](causal-view-binding.ts): five latest port values, explicit `unavailable` ports, observation cleanup | You need a different observation policy; the [ordinary panel](causal-ordinary-panel.ts) shows a consumer |"},{"line":35,"text":"| A Graph and prepared creation inputs | [`spendingAlertsFor`](causal-entry.ts): immutable defaults, per-compose overrides and returned view/capabilities | You also own input preparation or the executing host; follow [inputs](causal-inputs.ts) or [host](causal-focused-host.ts) for those responsibilities |"},{"line":36,"text":"| Issued capabilities, their owning Graph and expected binding | [`assertCausalCapabilities`](../../packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/capabilities.ts): issued-object, Graph, binding and lineage validation | You implement capability construction; the [role examples](causal-audience.examples.ts) show consumption |"},{"line":37,"text":"| The owning Graph and a running instance | [Inspect one instance in a shared graph](#inspect-one-instance-in-a-shared-graph): full structure plus that instance's host and retained evidence | You are tracing a specific readiness, admission or outcome dependency |"},{"line":38,"text":""},{"line":39,"text":"Using an existing view does not require reconstructing its input facts, permission"},{"line":40,"text":"sources or host. requests.explanation:
The handoff is a validate-then-deliver function. `assertCausalCapabilities(graph, capability, expected)` is the only admission gate: it looks the object up in the module-private `issued` WeakMap and throws `TypeError("causal capability binding mismatch")` when the object was never issued (a structural copy or cast), when `root.graph !== graph`, when `root.level !== "full"`, or when contract/implementationRevision/scope/epoch differ from the expected binding (packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/capabilities.ts:66-82). It then throws `TypeError("causal capability lineage mismatch")` unless each of `identity`, `execution`, `retained` is itself an issued handle of the same instance and Graph (capabilities.ts:83-87), and `TypeError("causal capability lower handle mismatch")` unless `execution.identity === identity` and `retained.execution === execution` (capabilities.ts:88-89). Because the assertion runs before `recipient(...)`, a structural copy, a different-Graph capability or a wrong binding never reaches the recipient; the README states the same rule: "A capability validation failure must be handled before passing the capabilities to a recipient; a structural copy is not an issued object" (examples/spending-alerts/README.md:41-43).

Delivery preserves identity relationships by passing the original frozen handles, not copies: `createCausalCapabilities` builds `identity`, `execution` (with `identity` nested), `retained` (with `execution` nested) and `full` as frozen objects and registers each level in the WeakMap (capabilities.ts:122-147). The demo asserts exactly these relationships after handoff: `execution === app.capabilities.execution`, `execution.identity === app.capabilities.identity`, `app.capabilities.retained.execution === execution` (examples/spending-alerts/causal-graded-demo.ts:85-87), and the framework example returns `capabilities.execution` unchanged after validation (examples/spending-alerts/causal-audience.examples.ts:17-25). The binding itself is validated/normalized by `causalBinding` (capabilities.ts:53-64), and the preset constructs the expected binding with `contract: "contract-v2"`, `implementationRevision: "construction-v1"`, `scope: "full"`, `epoch: binding.compositionEpoch` (examples/spending-alerts/causal-preset.ts:114-119).

Possession of the execution level does NOT authorize an arbitrary I/O call. `ExecutionCapability` exposes only graph Nodes (`terminals`, `conservation`, `causalQuiescence`) plus the identity handles (capabilities.ts:27-32); there is no write/open/execute method. The README says "Capabilities have no arbitrary I/O execution method" (README.md:94), and the audience example comments "an execution view grants no I/O method" (causal-audience.examples.ts:17). Actual I/O is gated elsewhere: the resource lease must be `transferred` before `write` is allowed (examples/spending-alerts/causal-resource.ts:76-79), and admission requires a matching local grant, current policy watermark, and ready inbox slot (examples/spending-alerts/causal-admission.ts:253-296). So the execution level is an observation/lineage handle, not an authorization token; a name or handle is not permission (README.md:86, 122-123).

### Choose the boundary you already have
These helpers are consumer-private source imports, **not published package
subpaths**. Start with the object supplied to your component:
| You already have | Read this contract first | Read implementation details when |

| An existing `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback | [`mountSpendingView`](causal-view-binding.ts): five latest port values, explicit `unavailable` ports, observation cleanup | You need a different observation policy; the [ordinary panel](causal-ordinary-panel.ts) shows a consumer |

| Issued capabilities, their owning Graph and expected binding | [`assertCausalCapabilities`](../../packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/capabilities.ts): issued-object, Graph, binding and lineage validation | You implement capability construction; the [role examples](causal-audience.examples.ts) show consumption |

| The owning Graph and a running instance | [Inspect one instance in a shared graph](#inspect-one-instance-in-a-shared-graph): full structure plus that instance's host and retained evidence | You are tracing a specific readiness, admission or outcome dependency |

instances, A and B, in the same Graph: A waits for its simulated result while the
panel switches to B; B succeeds without settling A; A then completes while its
panel is detached, and reconnecting does not write again. Expect

| Did this node's implementation change despite unchanged ID/edges? | Revision-bound source mapping within its declared coverage |
| Who changed it? | Separate provenance; an implementation digest alone gives no attribution |
| Which consequences remain unchanged? | Independent verification bound to the current revision and inputs |

receipt does not verify a new implementation. Existing bounded source-change and
mutation evidence can be inspected in the [implementation review](../../docs/design/causal-graded-entry-implementation/README.md).
Those retained artifacts describe their own revisions; the new demo does not
requalify them or attest the loaded production source.
The example and offline tests demonstrate available composition paths, not a
human usability result or superiority to a complete plain-code host. B121's real
inbox qualification, independent human/agent comparisons and aggregate acceptance

An unknown or reconciliation-required outcome is not success or"},{"line":150,"text":"proof of no submission, and it prevents normal-end readiness. The application"},{"line":151,"text":"must preserve those records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery."},{"line":152,"text":""},{"line":153,"text":"The ordinary panel does not poll diagnostics or claim that the whole run ended."},{"line":154,"text":"The protocol has no END message: business stop, node COMPLETE and run termination"},{"line":155,"text":"are distinct. An unknown or reconciliation-required outcome is not success or"},{"line":150,"text":"proof of no submission, and it prevents normal-end readiness. The application"},{"line":151,"text":"must preserve those records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery."},{"line":152,"text":""},{"line":153,"text":"The ordinary panel does not poll diagnostics or claim that the whole run ended."},{"line":154,"text":"The protocol has no END message: business stop, node COMPLETE and run termination"},{"line":155,"text":"are distinct. An unknown or reconciliation-required outcome is not success or"},{"line":150,"text":"proof of no submission, and it prevents normal-end readiness. The application"},{"line":151,"text":"must preserve those records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery."},{"line":152,"text":""},{"line":153,"text":"The ordinary panel does not poll diagnostics or claim that the whole run ended."},{"line":154,"text":"The protocol has no END message: business stop, node COMPLETE and run termination"},{"line":155,"text":"are distinct. An unknown or reconciliation-required outcome is not success or"},{"line":150,"text":"proof of no submission, and it prevents normal-end readiness. The application"},{"line":151,"text":"must preserve those records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery."},{"line":152,"text":""},{"line":153,"text":"The ordinary panel does not poll diagnostics or claim that the whole run ended."},{"line":154,"text":"The protocol has no END message: business stop, node COMPLETE and run termination"},{"line":155,"text":"are distinct. ## What the snippet does

`inspectSpendingInstance(graph, instance)` is a pure read. It takes the supplied `Graph` and the actual composed instance (the return value of `spendingAlertsFor(graph, defaults).compose(inputs)`, causal-entry.ts:49-77) and returns:

- `graph`: the **complete** owning Graph snapshot from `graph.describe()` with no `explain` filter, so nodes *and* edges are preserved (graph.ts:564-568; describe.ts:50-55). Counts or a filtered subgraph would discard the structure needed to investigate (README.md:117-118).
- `host`: the target's own `inspect()` records/readiness (causal-focused-host.ts:558-576), including `records` (request/admission/outcome, causal-focused-host.ts:47-51, 571-574), `inFlight`, `writes`, `dispatchStopped`, `fault`, `normalEndReady`.
- `readiness`: startup state from `instance.owner.startup.cache` (construction-scope.ts:18-24), owner `phase`, `runEndReady.cache` (causal-focused-host.ts:491-538), and the host's `normalEndReady` (causal-focused-host.ts:563-564).
- `publication`: `instance.view.publication.cache` — this instance's current publication, `undefined` before it publishes (README.md:111).
- `retainedQuiescence`: `instance.capabilities.retained.retainedQuiescence.cache` (capabilities.ts:33-37, 133-137; README.md:112).
- `authority`: `{ authorityId, authority }` where `authorityId = publication?.authorityId` and `authority = graph.find(authorityId)` (graph.ts:301-310). If the target has no publication, both are `undefined` — unavailable — even when another instance in the same Graph has published (README.md:113-123). No name-suffix scan is used; the exact id comes from this instance's publication.
- `correlatedRows`: each publication row joined to the host record with the same exact `requestRef` (causal-graded-demo.ts:207-238), so the two views can be compared without guessing.

## Detached display / locally quiet with unknown prior physical outcome

A detached panel only stops observation; the running instance keeps its outstanding obligations (README.md:143). Readiness is not termination: `startup` says `started` proves only that the instance started, not authorization, success or run completion (README.md:139), and `runEndReady`/`inspect().normalEndReady` are current readiness conditions, not proof that lifecycle termination or resource release occurred (README.md:144). The host's `normalEndReady` additionally requires `!fault && inFlight === 0 && !scheduled && !delivering && runEndReady.cache === true` (causal-focused-host.ts:563-564), and `runEndReady` itself requires a stop fact plus quiescence with no pending occurrences/effects and no `unknown`/`reconcile-required` outcomes (causal-focused-host.ts:517-535).

So with an unknown prior physical outcome: success cannot be concluded (only a matching `bytesWritten` establishes `succeeded`, causal-focused-host.ts:458-470); no-submit cannot be concluded either, because an unknown/reconciliation-required outcome is explicitly not proof of no submission and it prevents normal-end readiness (README.md:149-151). A safe replay also cannot be concluded from these reads alone: the host has one in-flight write, no queue and no automatic retry (README.md:146-149), and `unknown`/`reconcile-required` sets `dispatchStopped` (causal-focused-host.ts:224), so the retained record must be preserved rather than treated as recovered by panel cleanup (README.md:150-151).

## Why outcomes appear in two places, and why reads can differ

Host records retain request/admission/outcome and publish outcome facts into the Graph (README.md:125-128); the publication projects graph-held evidence (causal-publication.ts:61-80, `PublicationRow.recorded`). These are separate reads, not an atomic graph-and-host snapshot, so they may differ, and a missing publication does not mean no request was submitted (README.md:129-130). The exact `requestRef` is the join key: the demo asserts `publication.rows[0].proposal.requestRef` equals the retained record's `request.requestRef` and that `publication.rows[0].recorded` equals the host outcome state (causal-graded-demo.ts:210-211, 230). `correlatedRows` performs that same exact-reference join.

No transport invocation, no instance close, no fact emission, no topology change: only `describe()`, `find()`, `.cache` reads, `inspect()` and `owner`/`runEndReady` reads. Instance creation is not reimplemented; the second parameter accepts the real composed value. The snippet was not executed.

## Detached display / locally quiet with unknown prior physical outcome

A detached panel only stops observation; the running instance keeps its outstanding obligations (README.md:143). Readiness is not termination: `startup` says `started` proves only that the instance started, not authorization, success or run completion (README.md:139), and `runEndReady`/`inspect().normalEndReady` are current readiness conditions, not proof that lifecycle termination or resource release occurred (README.md:144). The host's `normalEndReady` additionally requires `!fault && inFlight === 0 && !scheduled && !delivering && runEndReady.cache === true` (causal-focused-host.ts:563-564), and `runEndReady` itself requires a stop fact plus quiescence with no pending occurrences/effects and no `unknown`/`reconcile-required` outcomes (causal-focused-host.ts:517-535).

So with an unknown prior physical outcome: success cannot be concluded (only a matching `bytesWritten` establishes `succeeded`, causal-focused-host.ts:458-470); no-submit cannot be concluded either, because an unknown/reconciliation-required outcome is explicitly not proof of no submission and it prevents normal-end readiness (README.md:149-151). A safe replay also cannot be concluded from these reads alone: the host has one in-flight write, no queue and no automatic retry (README.md:146-149), and `unknown`/`reconcile-required` sets `dispatchStopped` (causal-focused-host.ts:224), so the retained record must be preserved rather than treated as recovered by panel cleanup (README.md:150-151).

## Why outcomes appear in two places, and why reads can differ

Host records retain request/admission/outcome and publish outcome facts into the Graph (README.md:125-128); the publication projects graph-held evidence (causal-publication.ts:61-80, `PublicationRow.recorded`). These are separate reads, not an atomic graph-and-host snapshot, so they may differ, and a missing publication does not mean no request was submitted (README.md:129-130). The exact `requestRef` is the join key: the demo asserts `publication.rows[0].proposal.requestRef` equals the retained record's `request.requestRef` and that `publication.rows[0].recorded` equals the host outcome state (causal-graded-demo.ts:210-211, 230). `correlatedRows` performs that same exact-reference join.

## Constraints respected

No transport invocation, no instance close, no fact emission, no topology change: only `describe()`, `find()`, `.cache` reads, `inspect()` and `owner`/`runEndReady` reads. Instance creation is not reimplemented; the second parameter accepts the real composed value. The snippet was not executed.
